Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:CPO; Chief-Product-Officer; Product OwnerStellenbeschreibung:About HeyGermanyGermany urgently needs international talent. Yet complex and lengthy recognition processes prevent many qualified professionals from working in the jobs they trained for. At the same time, employers struggle to fill critical positions.HeyGermany wants to change that. We are building the digital infrastructure to make professional recognition and work integration faster and easier. We are starting with nursing and plan to expand into other regulated professions. Our mission is to remove bureaucratic barriers and help international talent access jobs that match their qualifications.The RoleWe are looking for a hands-on, product-driven Founding CTPO with the ambition to build HeyGermany as a co-founder. You will take full ownership of both product and technology, from understanding customer problems and defining our product vision to building, launching and scaling the solutions.You will work closely with the Founder & CEO to shape company strategy, identify growth opportunities and turn our vision into a product that users love and businesses are willing to pay for.We already have a live MVP (www.hey-germany.com (http://www.hey-germany.com) ), an initial recognition engine and talent pool, 400+ talent pool conversions, our first enterprise pilot and secured public funding.Your challenge is to turn this foundation into a scalable, user-centric platform that can take HeyGermany from one profession to many, while building the product and technology capabilities to support long-term growth.What You’ll Do- Own our product vision, strategy and roadmap, translating customer needs, business goals and market insights into clear priorities and measurable outcomes.- Lead product discovery and development end-to-end, from user research, problem validation and prototyping to technical implementation, launch and iteration.- Own our technology strategy and architecture, building scalable systems for qualification recognition, document processing, workflow automation and talent matching.- Turn complex regulatory and bureaucratic processes into simple, intuitive digital experiences, with a strong focus on usability, customer value and conversion.- Stay hands-on in building the product, making key technical decisions across frontend, backend, APIs, data and cloud infrastructure while maintaining a high standard of product quality.- Identify and develop AI-powered product opportunities where they create real value, particularly in document analysis, structured data extraction, intelligent matching and workflow automation.- Work directly with international professionals, employers and domain experts to understand their needs, validate assumptions and continuously improve the product.- Define and track key product metrics, using data, user feedback and experimentation to drive product decisions, engagement, conversion and business outcomes.- Build and lead our future product and engineering team, establishing a strong culture of ownership, customer focus, speed and continuous learning.What We’re Looking For- We care less about your current title than about what you have built, your product judgment and the level of ownership you are ready to take.- 7+ years of experience in software engineering, product development or technical product leadership, with strong hands-on technical capabilities.- A degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.- A proven track record of building and shipping digital products end-to-end, ideally in a founder, founding engineer, product-minded CTO, technical product lead or similar role.- Strong product thinking, with the ability to identify real customer problems, validate solutions, prioritize effectively and balance user needs with business impact and technical feasibility.- Strong experience with a modern web stack, ideally TypeScript, React/Next.js, backend development, APIs, databases and cloud infrastructure.- Practical experience building with LLMs and modern AI systems, including RAG, agents and evaluations, and using AI effectively in product development and day-to-day work.- Experience with product discovery, user research, UX principles, product analytics and iterative development. You know how to move from an initial hypothesis to a product that delivers measurable value.- The ability to make pragmatic decisions across product and technology, balancing speed, user experience, quality and scalability in an early-stage environment.- A strong understanding of how product decisions connect to business outcomes, including acquisition, activation, retention and monetization.- A founder mindset and strong connection to our mission**.** You want real ownership, are comfortable with the ambiguity of a pre-seed company and care about building a successful business, not just great technology.- Strong English communication skills are required. We are currently in conversations with investors for our next stage of growth.- The opportunity to work on a problem with tangible social and economic impact: helping international professionals access jobs that match their qualifications while helping employers access talent they urgently need.We believe professional opportunities should be determined by people’s skills, not by their ability to navigate bureaucracy.If you want to build both the product and the technology behind a company from the ground up, take real ownership and help shape HeyGermany as a co-founder, we would love to hear from you.Send us one product you've built that you're proud of, tell us what role you played in bringing it to life, and why this mission matters to you.katharina@hey-germany.com (https://mailto:katharina@hey-germany.com)Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: AURELIUS is a global alternative investor, distinguished and widely recognised for its operational approach. NPI & Industrialization- Collaborate with Operations on NPI program management from early involvement design, to design freeze through pilot, ramp, and stable serial production- Ensure early and structured involvement of NPI, Procurement, Manufacturing, and Quality in R&D projects- Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-cost, and design-for-serviceability discipline into every new program- Manage ramp readiness: supply readiness, test coverage, production line qualification, and yield curves5. At the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law, scholars pursue research relating to fundamental issues and current developments in the areas of public international law, European Union law, and the constitutional and administrative law of individual states, together with numerous visiting scholars from all over the world. In its fields, our library is the largest in Europe and one of the most comprehensive in the world.The newly established Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER), headed by Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg, invites applications for twoResearch Fellow positions (Doctoral Researchers) (x/f/m)with a preferred starting date of 1 January 2027 (the positions are funded for three years)The Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER) investigates how global order is transformed as states - particularly great and middle powers - pursue competing visions of the principles, rules and institutions that structure international relations amid intensifying geopolitical rivalry. The group conceptualizes these processes as constellations of global (dis)ordering through which states seek to advance their visions of order by creating, reshaping, connecting, bypassing, or disengaging from international institutions, building new formal or ad hoc institutional arrangements, and strategically leveraging economic and technological interdependence. DISORDER examines how such constellations emerge across the fields of security, economy, and technology, and what forms of global order they produce, transform, or erode.Job descriptionThe successful candidates will develop independent doctoral dissertation projects within the framework of the Max Planck Research Group “Constellations of Global (Dis)Ordering” (DISORDER). Their research should contribute to the group’s broader inquiry into how states pursue competing visions of global order through international institutions and how these processes reshape global order across different issue areas.Possible orientations of the doctoral projects include:- an actor-centred perspective, examining how a particular great or middle power pursues its vision of global order across different issue areas institutional settings; or- a domain-centred perspective, comparing how different states interact with and reshape international institutions within a particular field, such as security, economy, or technology.Potential empirical cases may include, but are not limited to, the United States, China, Russia, India, Brazil, Japan, and other international actors such as the European Union.The doctoral researchers will:- develop and conduct an original PhD project that contributes to the conceptual and empirical agenda of the DISORDER research group;- conduct empirical research using qualitative methods such as process tracing, qualitative content and discourse analysis, and semi-structured interviews;- contribute to the comparative and collaborative research activities of the group;- participate in research group meetings, workshops, conferences, and other academic activities;- present research findings at international conferences and prepare publications for peer-reviewed academic outlets;- contribute to the organization of workshops, conferences, and other activities of the research group and the MPIL.Your profile- An excellent Master’s degree or equivalent in Political Science, with a specialization in International Relations or Foreign Policy Analysis- A strong research interest in global order, international institutions, and great- and middle-power politics, including their foreign policies- A substantive interest in one or more of the group’s empirical issue areas (security, economy, and technology)- A strong interest in qualitative research and familiarity with relevant research methods- Excellent written and spoken English- Additional language skills and country- or region-specific expertise relevant to the proposed doctoral project are considered assets- The ability to conduct independent research while contributing actively to a collaborative research environmentWe offer- An attractive and international work environment with an unparalleled research infrastructure and a good working atmosphere- A varied, responsible and team-orientated job- Remuneration in accordance with the guidelines of the MPG funding agreements (65 per cent of EG13, TVöD-Bund)- Access to our world-leading library and a multitude of databases- A workplace that is easy to reach by public transport and free employee parking spaces- A job ticket for public transport- Offers for work-life balance and four affiliated daycare centresApplicationThe Max Planck Society has set itself the goal of employing more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where they are underrepresented. Women are therefore strongly encouraged to apply.Interested candidates are invited to submit their complete application exclusively via the online application system (https://jobs.mpil.de/3vrp7) available on our website by 22 November 2026.Applications should include a CV, a cover letter of no more than two pages, copies of relevant degree certificates and transcripts of records, a one-page summary of the applicant’s Master’s thesis, a five-page PhD project proposal that clearly relates to the research agenda of the DISORDER group and indicates which of the thematic orientations outlined above the proposed project primarily addresses, and two letters of recommendationThe documents will be deleted after the application process. The interviews will take place in late November/early December in person at the Max Planck Institute for Comparative Public Law and International Law in Heidelberg. Application expenses cannot be covered.For questions regarding the positions, please contact Dr. Gordon Friedrichs at friedrichs@mpil.de (https://mailto:friedrichs@mpil.de) .
